summary: Very concentrated: 4 holdings, the top ten are 100% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 279% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 0.4 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are cheaper, more profitable, slower-growing and smaller.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 5 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1971; a medical doctor (Vanderbilt) who began writing about value investing online in 1996. Founded Scion Capital in 2000, closed it in 2008, and reopened as Scion Asset Management in 2013.
profile.approach: Deep-value and contrarian: large bets against the crowd, including via options, and frequent changes of position.
known: Bet against US subprime mortgages from 2005 with credit default swaps, making about $100 million for himself and over $700 million for investors; told in The Big Short.
Disclosed put options on Nvidia and Palantir in 2025, then withdrew Scion from SEC registration in November 2025, effectively closing the fund.
profile.note: No new 13F filings are expected after Scion's 2025 deregistration; the last one covers September 2025.
